---
title: "Getting Started"
---

captain-hook turns the guardrails you want into typed, testable Python: a hook is an
event, some conditions, an action, and a verdict Claude Code has to obey. It also reads
the corrections you give Claude and opens pull requests that codify the durable ones as
new hooks. These pages go from nothing to a tested hook firing in Claude Code, in order.
Every snippet is copy-pasteable, and every command runs through `uvx capt-hook …` (no
install). When you want to *look something up* instead, switch to the
[Reference](../reference/index.qmd).

Pick your entry point:

- To set up in one command, run `uvx capt-hook init` — see [Installation](installation.qmd).
- To let Claude do it, install the plugin and ask it to "set up captain hook" — see [Agent Skills](skills.qmd).
- To block one command in 5 minutes, jump straight to the [Quickstart](quickstart.qmd).
- To build the mental model first, read [How Hooks Work](../guide/how-it-works.qmd).
- To let captain-hook learn hooks from your corrections, see the [Session reviewer](../guide/session-reviewer.qmd).
- To copy a working hook into your repo, browse the [Examples](../examples/index.qmd).
